_comment: All policy thresholds live here so the agent's behavior can be tuned and audited without touching code. Each value has a stated justification for defense in review.

cooldown_days.justification: Real B2B dunning cycles typically space contacts 5-7 days apart; contacting more frequently reads as harassment and increases annoyance penalty disproportionately.

max_contact_attempts.justification: Caps runaway auto-escalation. After 4 attempts an invoice moves to 'exhausted' status for manual review instead of continuing to auto-contact indefinitely -- this is the bounded/gated requirement.

min_attempts_before_phone_call.justification: Cannot go straight to a phone call; at least one reminder (gentle or firm) must be attempted first.

min_attempts_before_payment_plan_offer.justification: Payment plan offer is a relationship-preserving escalation and should only follow at least one prior contact showing the invoice remains unresolved.

escalate_collections_gate.justification: Escalation to collections is the most relationship-damaging action. It is only permitted if a payment plan was already offered and ignored, OR the invoice is severely overdue (60+ days) with at least 2 prior contact attempts already made.

human_approval_policy.justification: Low-importance customers can be auto-escalated to keep the pipeline moving. Any customer with importance_score >= 0.3 (Standard tier and above) requires a logged human approval before escalate_collections fires, since relationship damage on valuable customers has outsized business cost.

repeated_ignore_escalation_rule.justification: If the same action-tier fails twice in a row, repeating it a third time is wasted effort and unnecessary annoyance -- the next action must move at least one intensity tier up.
